targetWords.definition: To absorb a liquid means to take it inside.
targetWords.example: He used a sponge to absorb the water on the floor.

targetWords.definition: — My boss is a nice person.
A committee is a group of people who meet together to make decisions.
targetWords.example: ■The school's committee agreed on a new dress code for students.

targetWords.definition: A contract is a written agreement between two people.
targetWords.example: The woman signed a contract when she bought the house.

targetWords.definition: A crew is a group of workers.
targetWords.example: ■My father has a crew. They help him build houses.

targetWords.definition: To devote time to something means to spend a lot of time doing it.
targetWords.example: ■She devotes two hours a day to playing the piano.
■My dog digs in the yard so he can hide his bones.

targetWords.definition: To dine means to eat dinner.
targetWords.example: The young couple dined at their home.

targetWords.definition: To donate is to give something to a charity or organization.
targetWords.example: We donate money to Christmas charities every year.

targetWords.definition: If something is double, it is twice as much, or twice as many.
targetWords.example: I paid almost double the amount for that shirt.

targetWords.definition: To elevate something is to put it at a higher level.
targetWords.example: The man elevated the picture so he could see it better.

targetWords.definition: A flavor is the taste of food or drinks.
targetWords.example: The flavor of the ice cream was very good.

targetWords.definition: A foundation is a group that provides money for research.
targetWords.example: ■The foundation raised money to give scholarships to students.

targetWords.definition: A generation is a group of people who live at the same time.
targetWords.example: My grandparents are from a different generation than me.

targetWords.definition: A handle is the part of an object people hold while using it.
targetWords.example: The pot is very hot. So pick it up by the handle.

targetWords.definition: A layer covers over something or is between two things.
targetWords.example: ■There was a layer of snow on the tops of the houses this morning.
My brother played rugby in the mud. Now he's dirty.

targetWords.definition: If something is smooth, it has no bumps.
targetWords.example: The baby's skin felt very smooth.

story.title: The Lucky Knife
story.passage:
I've devoted my life to studying past generations. Last year, I had a unique

chance to work with my uncle. Our job was to find old treasures for a school's

history foundation. He also hired a crew of students. They signed a contract to

work with him. He was the boss. The place was strange, though. I dined on many

things that I had never tasted before. They had an unusual flavor.

We had been there about a month and hadn't found anything. One day, I

began to dig in the soil. The ground's layers got wetter. Soon I was digging in

the mud. My shovel began to get very heavy. It felt like it had doubled in weight

because the ground had absorbed a lot of water.

Finally, I saw something in the mud. It was an old knife! The handle felt

smooth in my hand. I elevated it so I could see it better. There was writing on it.

" It says it will bring good luck," my uncle said with a smile. "Why don't you

keep it?"

I put it in my tent. The next day, we found many more things. There were pots,

jewelry and weapons. My uncle donated all of the things to a special committee.

Many newspapers wrote stories about it. It seemed the knife really did bring

good luck!
